head: 1Password hacked: names and emails taken, passwords and vaults safe
dek: 1Password says an attacker got into an employee's work GitHub account on 19 November and downloaded account records for some customers, including names and email addresses. Vault contents, the keys that protect them and recovery keys weren't accessed.
details: The attacker used the account to reach 1Password's source code, push malicious code to backend services and get into its build system. The records also held account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, login protocol data and tokens in some invitation and recovery emails; users with pending invites or recovery were told directly. 1Password doesn't store account passwords or Secret Keys. It has rotated its internal credentials, made invitation and recovery codes ten characters long instead of six digits, and brought in outside security experts.
means: If you use 1Password, your saved passwords weren't exposed, but your name and email may be in the attacker's hands, so fake 1Password emails, texts or calls are more likely.
todo: 1Password says you don't need to change anything in your account. Don't answer messages about 1Password, invitations or account recovery that you didn't start; type your password and Secret Key only into the 1Password app or its website, opened yourself. Report anything odd to support@1password.com.
